_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.note: Many physics textbooks wrongly blame the Tacoma Narrows collapse on resonance. Billah and Scanlan wrote a 1991 paper in the American Journal of Physics saying so.
A 2,800 foot main span, stiffened by eight foot deep plate girders. An earlier proposal had called for 25 foot deep trusses.

beats.text: Not a storm. Around 42 miles per hour.
beats.note: Structure magazine reports winds near 42 mph that morning. Other accounts give about 40.
Vortex shedding would have come at about 1 Hz, but the bridge was twisting at about 0.2 Hz when it failed, according to Structure.

beats.text: The wind fed the twisting itself.
beats.note: Aeroelastic flutter. The bridge's shape drew energy from the wind, so the motion grew rather than staying bounded.

beats.context: The wind recorded that morning, reported by Structure magazine. A steady breeze was enough.

beats.text: The bridge was not shaken apart. It was pushed into shaking itself.
